title: 9/11 at 25: How Russia Turned 9/11 Into Strategic Opportunity
gist: Podcast notes: Anna Borshchevskaya argues Russia exploited Washington's post-9/11 belief that Moscow could be a genuine counterterrorism partner, gaining long-term strategic advantage over the West, while itself having a long pattern of propping up terrorism dating to the Soviet era.

themes.theme: Russia's exploitation of the War on Terror

insights.claim: Putin was the first foreign leader to call President George W. Bush with condolences on 9/11.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Illustrates how early gestures shaped a US misperception of Russia as a partner.
insights.quote: President Vladimir Putin was the first foreign leader to call President George W. Bush

insights.claim: Washington's belief, before and for years after 9/11, that Russia could be a legitimate counterterrorism partner was naivety that Moscow exploited to its long-term strategic advantage against the West.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Argues for skepticism toward cooperative framings with Moscow in current negotiations.
insights.quote: Anna Borshchevskaya argues Russia exploited that naivety to its long-term strategic advantage against the West

insights.claim: Moscow has a long pattern of propping up terrorism around the world dating back to the Soviet Union.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Frames Russia as a sponsor rather than a counterterrorism ally, relevant to sanctions and Middle East policy.
insights.quote: Moscow's own long pattern of propping up terrorism around the world, dating back to the Soviet Union
